Our solution.

Throughline. Find your conference, say your goal in your own words, and get your path: what to learn first, in what order, and where to learn it before the talk starts. It remembers what you know, and every answer is explained. It's powered by a FalkorDB knowledge graph, and live web data from Bright Data.

What we achieved with FalkorDB.

Why a graph? Our data is connections: talks require and teach concepts, concepts depend on concepts, and attendees know concepts. And our questions are paths, with time rules: what do I need before this talk, and what do those need? In tables, that's recursive joins. In FalkorDB, it's one traversal.

The schema. Depends-on links are derived from talks that teach one concept and require another. 'Prepares you for' is a traversal: a talk, what it teaches, and the later talks that require it. The agent answers only through thirteen graph tools, and its own Cypher is read-only, on a copy with no attendee data.

caption: The real Cypher behind an answer, from the demo
voiceover: And every answer shows the real Cypher it ran.

The results: 125 talks, 55 concepts, 491 relationships, and 227 prepares-you-for links. The multi-hop prerequisite query takes 66 milliseconds on the hosted lab; a full day plan, about 1.6 seconds. Memory makes it personal: four steps for a newcomer, one with experience. And 400 of 401 extracted links passed the word-for-word check.
How we used Bright Data.

Why Bright Data? The data we need is live, and hard to reach. The schedule page renders with JavaScript, so a plain fetch gets no sessions. And conferences near you, and good readings, need live Google results that a basic script can't reliably get.

The pipeline. The Browser API loads the schedule and records its data feed, and OpenAI extracts concepts, with word-for-word evidence, into FalkorDB. The SERP API runs three searches for your city; we keep only conferences from returned links, check dates in code, and merge and cache the results. Search results also become vetted readings and explainers, stored in the graph.

The results. Freshness: a live re-scrape on the hackathon morning found two dropped talks, two new ones and a corrected abstract, and the graph was updated. Scale: all 125 talks, with 434 vetted readings. Quality: only returned URLs, dates checked in code, and the last good snapshot kept if a scrape looks broken.
Throughline: find your conference, say your goal, and walk in ready. Try it live at the link on screen. Thanks for watching.
